subject: Day 14: first growth spurt; EPDS screening; open the 529
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 14. The first common growth spurt opens this week. Expect 24-48 hours of unusually frequent feeding (cluster feeding), then a reset. Anushka's milk supply, if breastfeeding, calibrates to demand during this window. Resist the urge to supplement reflexively, but do not ignore signs of insufficient transfer.

Action items
- Take the EPDS (Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale) screening for Anushka this week if her OB has not administered it. A score above 10 warrants a call to her OB or PCP; a score of 13 or higher traditionally distinguishes likely depression. ACOG Committee Opinion 757 on perinatal depression screening: https://www.acog.org/clinical/clinical-guidance/committee-opinion/articles/2018/11/screening-for-perinatal-depression. See baby-kb/mom/ppd-watch-fors.md.
- Open the 529 plan once Avi's SSN has arrived (typical mail timing is 2-4 weeks post-birth). Plan selection in baby-kb/dad/finances-529.md. Front-loading the early years compounds maximally: $25,000 contributed at birth, growing at 7% real returns, becomes about $96,000 by age 18.
- Verify the insurance enrollment for Avi has actually processed. Call the insurer; do not trust that the form went through. Insurance companies do not retroactively cover the 1-month well visit if enrollment lapsed.
- Apply for paternity leave if not already on it. Coordinate with employer HR and California Paid Family Leave (up to 8 weeks). California EDD reference: https://edd.ca.gov/en/disability/paid-family-leave/. See baby-kb/dad/paternity-leave-optimization.md.
- Reorder postpartum supplies that are running low. Anushka is still in lochia rubra-to-serosa transition; pad supply matters.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Cluster feeding for 24-48 hours, fussiness in the evenings, increased need to be held. Normal during the spurt.
- [low concern] Baby acne (neonatal cephalic pustulosis) peaking around week 3-4; resolves on its own.
- [monitor] Baby blues in Anushka persisting beyond week 2. About 50-80% of mothers experience baby blues; resolution by 2 weeks postpartum is typical. Persistence escalates the concern toward postpartum depression. CDC overview: https://www.cdc.gov/reproductive-health/depression/index.html
- [call within 24h] Forceful projectile vomiting after most feeds with weight stagnation (pyloric stenosis: typically male, first-born, presents weeks 3-6, surgical correction).
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F in an infant under 90 days. Apnea (a breathing pause longer than 20 seconds, or any pause with a color change). Seizure activity. Call 911 for blue lips or unresponsiveness.

Enrichment opportunity
Mirror play: hold Avi in front of a mirror for 30-60 seconds during an awake-alert window. He is not recognizing himself yet, but the face-tracking response is the active ingredient; face-perception circuitry is tuning. Sustained eye contact during feeds will also start appearing this week.

Upcoming
- Day 14-21: first common growth spurt (cluster feeding 24-48h).
- Day 28-35: 1-month well visit window opens; first social smile typically emerges.
- Day 35-42: peak of the PURPLE crying curve at about 6 weeks corrected age.
- Day 42: Anushka's 6-week postpartum visit (clearance for exercise and intimacy usually granted here).

Source
baby-kb/buckets/week-03.md, baby-kb/mom/ppd-watch-fors.md, baby-kb/dad/finances-529.md, and baby-kb/dad/paternity-leave-optimization.md.
